summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a focused demo of rate limiting, quotas, and org/project key controls in the Console and API. Northbridge is evaluating for a proof-of-concept; main concerns were per-project isolation, key rotation, SSO/SAML, and burst capacity. Next step is pricing and POC scheduling.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Li (Redwood SE), Laura Jensen (Northbridge - Dir Eng), Tom Reyes (Northbridge SRE), Mika Suzuki (Northbridge - Head Security)

[00:00] Samira Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro \u0014 I'm Samira, AE on the account, and Ethan is our SE who will run the console/API demo.
[00:12] Laura Jensen: Hi all, thanks. We scheduled this to see how your org/project keys and rate limiting would map to our multi-tenant architecture.
[00:18] Ethan Li: Awesome. We'll jump into the Console demo and then show API examples, and we'll touch on Optimize suggestions for batching and caching too. If we run through too fast call out and we'll pause.
[00:32] Tom Reyes: Great, we're especially interested in per-team quotas and how key scoping works. We have several products that share the same org but need strict project isolation.
[00:40] Mika Suzuki: Also from security: key rotation, KMS integration, and audit logs. We'll need those to sign off.
[00:46] Ethan Li: Totally, we'll demo org-level and project-level keys, RBAC, and the audit trail. Quick qual question \u0014 what's your current stack? Are you on k8s in GCP?
[00:58] Laura Jensen: Yes, GKE, internal services talk to public APIs through a gateway. We try to minimize token sharing; currently we use a single API key per product but it's messy.
[01:10] Samira Khan: Understood. And timeline? are you looking to run a POC in the next month?
[01:13] Laura Jensen: Ideally yes, end of April, depending on procurement.

[01:20] Ethan Li: Ok jumping into the Console \u0014 (screen share) \u0014 top level org view. You can see org-level quotas and default project quotas, and you can create project keys scoped to routes, e.g., embeddings-only, generation-only.
[01:35] Ethan Li: I'll create a new project key: "billing-team-project". Scope it to the embeddings endpoint and set a per-minute quota of 60k tokens, daily cap 1.5M tokens. We'll also enable key rotation every 30 days.
[01:50] Tom Reyes: Does rotation happen automatically? how do we push to our secrets manager?
[01:56] Ethan Li: Yes you can enable automatic rotation; we integrate with KMS/HSM providers \u0014 there's a webhook and a secrets sync to common vaults. Might be named slightly different in the UI, sometimes shows "K M S" in transcriptions, but the flow is there.
[02:12] Laura Jensen: And for burst traffic, like when many users hit chat concurrently, how do you handle short bursts without dropping requests?
[02:20] Ethan Li: Good question. We use token-bucket style lease plus a burst window. You can configure per-project burst allowance and global fallback policies that route to a lower-capacity model rather than returning 429s. For critical routes we recommend a small reserved capacity in Dedicated.
[02:37] Samira Khan: To add, our smart routing can failover to compatible model variants in another region if capacity constraints hit. That keeps apps online while preserving SLAs.

[02:46] Laura Jensen: In procurement we've got strict cost controls \u0014 can we enforce quotas per team and also get per-token billing?
[02:53] Samira Khan: Yes \u0014 Console has per-key metering and token-level cost breakdowns. You can export per-route cost reports and set alerts when a project is nearing budget.
[03:05] Tom Reyes: How granular are the quotas \u0014 can we do concurrency vs token-rate?
[03:09] Ethan Li: We support multiple quota dimensions: tokens per minute, requests per minute, concurrent requests. You can combine them with priority policies; for instance, limit concurrency to protect tail latencies while allowing token throughput for streaming.

[03:24] Mika Suzuki: On audit logs \u0014 do you store full request payloads? that would be sensitive PHI in our use case.
[03:30] Ethan Li: By default logs are metadata-only; full payload logging is opt-in and can be routed to your VPC or SIEM. For Private deployments we can keep logs on-prem. We also redact PII on ingestion if needed.
[03:43] Mika Suzuki: Good. Can you show the API for creating project keys? we'd like to script onboarding.
[03:47] Ethan Li: Sure. (switches tabs) The API is a simple POST to /v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/keys with scope and quota body. Here's an example payload...
[03:58] Ethan Li: "scope": ["chat.generate"], "quotas": {"tokens_per_minute": 20000, "daily_tokens": 1000000} \u0014 apologies transcripts sometimes merge braces, but gist is you declare scopes and quota buckets.
[04:15] Laura Jensen: Is there a CLI? we prefer IaC.
[04:18] Samira Khan: Yes, we have terraform and cli plugins to manage orgs/projects/keys. Many customers use IaC to onboard projects so keys are created as part of deployment.

[04:28] Tom Reyes: What happens when a project goes over quota? immediate 429? throttled?
[04:32] Ethan Li: You can choose behavior per policy: hard reject with 429, soft throttle with degraded quality model, or queue and apply backpressure. For internal services we usually recommend soft throttle plus alerting.

[04:45] Laura Jensen: Any rate-limiting at route-level \u0014 like for embeddings endpoints to stop a noisy neighbor?
[04:50] Ethan Li: Yes, route-level policies can be attached to keys. You can also set shared budgets across projects or set differential weights per route (e.g., embeddings cost X tokens).

[05:02] Samira Khan: Quick note on Optimize \u0014 it will analyze your traffic and recommend batching, caching, and quantization profiles to lower unit costs. That ties into rate limiting because it can suggest changing quotas or batch sizes for better throughput.

[05:15] Ethan Li: I'm going to demo a quick POC scenario \u0014 say you want a per-customer sub-project with a low-latency SLA. We'll create project, apply RBAC so only billing-team admins can change quotas, then attach a reserved capacity policy.
[05:28] Ethan Li: (typing) Creating project "cust-1234"... attaching reserved pool 1: 2x A100s for dedicated, burst pool enabled. Setting a per-minute token limit and concurrency limit.
[05:45] Tom Reyes: Are reserved pools billed differently? we need predictability.
[05:48] Samira Khan: Reserved capacity is commit-based \u0014 monthly/annual \u0014 so you get predictable throughput and cost. Host tier is usage-based.

[05:59] Laura Jensen: On SSO \u0014 do you support SAML and SCIM for user provisioning?
[06:03] Ethan Li: Yes SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC maps to your identity provider groups.

[06:10] Mika Suzuki: For encryption, can we bring our own KMS keys?
[06:13] Samira Khan: Yes, BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated, and hosted can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping.

[06:20] Laura Jensen: Any limits on number of project keys? we have hundreds of microservices that would each have their own key.
[06:25] Ethan Li: No hard limit; recommended patterns are one key per service or per environment. Console supports bulk key creation via API/CLI.

[06:35] (demo continues, Ethan shows console screenshots and rate-limit policy JSON examples)

[07:02] Ethan Li: I'm switching to the live logs \u0014 here you can see per-key token consumption, per-route latency percentiles, and alerts. For noisy neighbors we typically set a rate-limited rule with spike protection.
[07:15] Tom Reyes: The logs UI looks good; can we stream those to Grafana or DataDog?
[07:19] Ethan Li: Yes, we have exporters and webhooks. You can plug into your observability stack. Some customers use our retention + export for the first 30 days while analytics team gets set up.

[07:32] Laura Jensen: For the POC we'd want to validate: 1) key scoping and rotation, 2) quota enforcement under load, 3) integration with our KMS and SSO, 4) cost visibility. Does that align with what you typically run?
[07:44] Samira Khan: Exactly. Our standard POC is a week of benchmarking with a small reserved pool, we provide test harness scripts and a report.

[07:52] Mika Suzuki: On the compliance side we'd like early access to SOC 2 docs and a summary of data residency.
[07:57] Samira Khan: We'll send the SOC2 pack and a note about on-prem/private deployment for EU data residency.

[08:04] (brief cross-talk and clarifications about rate-limit metrics naming \u0014 e.g., tokens/min vs tps)

[08:16] Ethan Li: One gotcha to call out \u0014 when you use advanced batching from Optimize, burst patterns can change; we recommend running a dry-run with your traffic to tune quotas, because batching can make token peaks more spiky if many requests collate.
[08:31] Tom Reyes: Noted. Our SRE will want the scripts.

[08:36] Laura Jensen: Who handles the contract? procurement or sales?
[08:40] Samira Khan: I'll handle initial pricing and procurement introduction. For Dedicated or Private we'll loop in contracts and solutions.

[08:46] Ethan Li: Any other technical questions?

[08:49] Tom Reyes: How do you handle deprecated keys? auto-revoke?

[08:52] Ethan Li: Keys can be scheduled for deactivation; rotation can supersede them and we keep audit trails. You can also have a grace window where old key works while clients rotate.

[09:05] Laura Jensen: Ok let's recap next steps.

[09:08] Samira Khan: We'll send pricing and SOC2/security docs. Ethan will send console screenshots and the demo recording plus API examples and terraform snippets. Northbridge to confirm POC week (they were aiming for Apr 20).

[09:19] Laura Jensen: Sounds good. We'll confirm internal stakeholders and get back by Thursday.

[09:24] Mika Suzuki: I'll review the security docs and flag any blockers.

[09:28] Samira Khan: Thanks everybody \u0014 we'll follow up by email with the artifacts.

[09:32] (meeting ends)

Notes on quality: transcription had occasional label mixups and some code-snippet braces flattened; content verified by SE after meeting recording.
